skill.name: server-management
skill.description: Server management guidance for production operations, including process supervision, monitoring, logs, health checks, scaling, and basic hardening principles.
skill.summary: Plan safer production operations with practical server management decision frameworks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns, and the reviewed skill is prompt-only guidance for server operations. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable behavior was found in SKILL.md.

content.user_title: Manage Production Servers with Clear Principles
content.value_statement: Production servers fail when teams rely on ad hoc checks and manual recovery. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reason about operations choices.
actual_capabilities: Compares process management options such as PM2, systemd, containers, and orchestration tools.
Defines monitoring categories for availability, performance, errors, and server resources.
Explains log rotation, structured logging, log levels, and sensitive data handling.
Guides scaling decisions based on CPU, memory, response time, and traffic patterns.
Prioritizes troubleshooting steps across processes, logs, resources, networks, and dependencies.
Summarizes core server security practices for access, firewall rules, patches, secrets, and audits.
limitations: It teaches operational decision-making, not exact command syntax for every platform.
It does not connect to servers, inspect live metrics, or change infrastructure by itself.
It cannot replace organization-specific incident procedures, compliance rules, or access policies.
It provides general guidance that must be adapted to each production environment.

use_cases.title: Plan a new service launch
use_cases.description: Choose process management, health checks, monitoring, and logging before a service reaches production.

use_cases.title: Improve operational readiness
use_cases.description: Review whether existing services have crash recovery, alerts, log rotation, and basic hardening.

use_cases.title: Triage production symptoms
use_cases.description: Follow a structured order for checking process state, logs, resources, network behavior, and dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Review a server setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment of a small production service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this server setup and identify missing basics for process management, monitoring, logs, health checks, and security. Keep recommendations practical.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a process manager
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate selection between common runtime options.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare PM2, systemd, containers, and orchestration for this application. Recommend one option and explain the tradeoffs for restarts, reloads, clustering, and persistence.

prompt_templates.title: Design monitoring and alerts
prompt_templates.scenario: Operational planning for a growing service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a monitoring plan for this service. Include availability, performance, error, and resource metrics with alert severity levels and tool suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan scaling and incident response
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for production growth and reliability.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these production symptoms and propose a scaling and troubleshooting plan. Separate quick fixes from durable changes, and include health check considerations.

output_examples.input: A Node.js API runs on one virtual machine and is restarted manually after crashes.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a process manager, crash restart policy, persistent startup configuration, basic uptime checks, and log rotation before traffic grows.

output_examples.input: A service has slow responses during traffic spikes, high CPU, and limited monitoring.
output_examples.output: The response prioritizes profiling, CPU and response-time alerts, horizontal scaling options, and a clear warning versus critical alert strategy.

output_examples.input: An on-call engineer sees intermittent failures but no clear incident checklist.
output_examples.output: The response orders checks by process state, logs, resources, network conditions, dependencies, and health check results.

best_practices: Provide the application type, hosting model, traffic profile, and current monitoring when asking for advice.
Ask for tradeoffs between simple tools and managed platforms before changing production operations.
Validate any recommendation against your incident policy, access model, and compliance requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for one universal command sequence without describing the service and environment.
Do not treat scaling as the first answer before checking profiling, logs, and resource data.
Do not copy generic security guidance without confirming ports, users, secrets, and patch responsibilities.

faq.question: Does this skill run server commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for server management decisions and does not execute commands by itself.

faq.question: Which process managers does it discuss?
faq.answer: It covers PM2, systemd, containers, Kubernetes, and Docker Swarm at a decision-making level.

faq.question: Can it help design monitoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It organizes monitoring around availability, performance, errors, and resource usage.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights SSH keys, firewall limits, security patches, secret handling, and audit logging.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for an SRE runbook?
faq.answer: No. It can help draft and review runbook logic, but teams must add environment-specific procedures.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it for production planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives Claude Code and Codex structured prompts for server operations reasoning.
